title: Validator defect after valid expensive outputs
original_authorship: Original discovery fixture reconstructed from archived mechanism IDs; not copied from a historical model response.
artifact: Thirty expensive analysis outputs were generated, hashed, and manually spot-checked as valid. A reporting validator rejects all of them because it accepts the field label 'risk_summary' but the frozen request allowed the semantically equivalent label 'risk synopsis'. A proposed recovery deletes the accepted outputs and reruns all thirty analyses.
review_request: Review the proposed recovery and identify what should be repaired or revalidated.
expected_material_mechanism: The defect is in validation or transport, not in the accepted substantive outputs.
Repair the smallest defective layer and revalidate the preserved outputs.
Replay is justified only if deterministic evidence shows the outputs themselves are stale, invalid, or bound to the wrong inputs.
acceptable_alternative_findings: Patch the validator to honor the frozen request contract.
Reconstruct missing receipt fields from accepted deterministic facts.
Reopen only the smallest phase proven invalid.
prohibited_false_positives: Preserve outputs after a real input, identity, freshness, or hash mismatch.
Treat receipt prose as stronger than primary evidence.
Require broad recomputation merely for additional confidence.
dangerous_failures: Destroy valid expensive outputs and repeat the full generation batch.
Approve the report without fixing or validating the defective layer.
notes: Tests repair-only recovery without protecting genuinely invalid work.
